Trump’s Approval Rating Falls
A new poll shows President Trump with an approval rating of 37%, down from 39%
, and a disapproval rating of 54%, down from 58%.
The Emerson College poll found that 56% of voters had an unfavorable view of the Republican Party and 35% had a favorable view.
The Democratic Party received a 44% favorable rating and a 47% unfavorable rating.
These ratings include responses from Democrats, Republicans and independents.
Over the past year, the Democratic Party’s favorable rating rose nine points, while the Republican Party’s favorable rating fell nine points and its unfavorable rating rose 12 points.
Top Voter Priorities

Addressing the cost of living ranked highest among the issues listed for Congress in 2027, with 57% of voters calling it a top priority. Other issues ranked as follows, by the percentage of voters calling each a top priority:
End of Iran War: 49%
Ban Stock Trading in Congress: 49%
Healthcare Reform: 45%
Regulating AI Industry: 37%

"Voters are most eager for Congress to address the cost of living: 71% of Democrats, 58% of independents, and 42% of Republicans think it should be the top priority for Congress in 2027," Emerson College Executive Director of Polling
Spencer Kimball
said.

title: Trump Approval Drops to 37% As Cost of Living Tops Voters' Priorities
